name: Al-Masmak Fortress
culture_note: 18th-century mudbrick citadel; the gate still bears the spearhead from the 1902 battle that reunified Saudi Arabia.

name: National Museum of Saudi Arabia
culture_note: Eight galleries charting the Arabian Peninsula from prehistoric times through the founding of the modern Kingdom.

name: Diriyah At-Turaif UNESCO District
culture_note: Birthplace of the Saudi state and a UNESCO World Heritage Site; mudbrick palaces and mosques dating to the 15th century.

name: Al-Bujairi Heritage Park
culture_note: Restored craftsmen's quarter directly across the wadi from At-Turaif; active art studios and traditional coffee houses.

name: Edge of the World (Jebel Fihrayn)
culture_note: 300-metre vertical escarpment overlooking the Tuwaiq valley — locals call it the end of the world.

name: King Abdulaziz Camel Market
culture_note: The world's largest camel market; thousands of camels traded daily. Go before 10am.

name: Al-Murabba Historical Palace
culture_note: 1930s mudbrick palace of King Abdulaziz, precursor to the modern capital.

name: Riyadh Art District (JAX District)
culture_note: Open-air public art installations along Riyadh's contemporary art district — distinct from Ithra, the King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture, which is in Dhahran.

name: Al-Zal Old Market
culture_note: Traditional bazaar unchanged since the 1940s; gold, spices, and antique silver.

name: Al-Balad UNESCO Historic District
culture_note: 400-year-old coral-stone houses with intricately carved wooden Rawasheen (balconies); UNESCO since 2014.

name: Al-Rahmah Floating Mosque
culture_note: Built on stilts over the Red Sea; appears to float at high tide. Open to non-Muslim visitors outside prayer times.

name: Abdul Raouf Khalil Museum
culture_note: Private collection covering 7,000 years of Arabian history across four floors; exceptional Islamic manuscript gallery.

name: Nasif Historical House
culture_note: 19th-century merchant mansion where King Abdulaziz stayed during his 1925 campaign; still preserves original furniture.

name: Al-Balad Flower & Spice Market
culture_note: Frankincense, oud, and saffron traded in the same alley for five centuries.

name: Hegra (Mada'in Salih) — Nabataean Tombs
culture_note: Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site; 111 rock-cut Nabataean tombs dating to the 1st century CE.

name: AlUla Old Town
culture_note: Abandoned 900-year-old mudbrick settlement; 900 homes, 400 shops, and six mosques awaiting rediscovery.

name: Jabal Ikmah (Library Mountain)
culture_note: Open-air library of Lihyanite, Dadanitic, and Minaic inscriptions carved into sandstone cliffs — over 500 ancient texts.

name: Dadan Archaeological Site
culture_note: Capital of the Lihyan and Dadanite kingdoms (9th–1st c. BCE); lion-carved tomb facades visible from the valley.

name: Maraya — Mirror Building
culture_note: World record-holder for largest mirror-clad building; 9,740 m² of mirrored facades reflecting the Ashar Valley canyon.

name: AlUla Oasis Palm Grove Walk
culture_note: Ancient falaj irrigation system still watering 2 million date palms; some trees are over 1,000 years old.

name: AlUla Date Farm Experience
culture_note: 70+ named date varieties; farmers still harvest by hand using the same climbing technique as their ancestors.

name: Dedan Ancient Kingdom Ruins
culture_note: Seat of the Lihyan kingdom; towering lion statues once flanked the entrance to the royal tombs.

name: Jabal Sawda
culture_note: The highest peak in Saudi Arabia at roughly 3,015m; cool highland air draws crowds fleeing the summer heat of the plains.

name: Shada Palace (Qasr Shada)
culture_note: Early 20th-century stone-and-timber palace, now a museum of Aseer regional heritage and costume.

name: Al-Muftaha Arts Village
culture_note: Cluster of artist studios and small galleries built into a former royal estate, showcasing Aseeri painting and Al-Qatt wall art.

name: Abha Lake Park
culture_note: A man-made lake and promenade at roughly 2,200m elevation, a favored evening gathering spot in the cool highland climate.

name: Habala Hanging Village
culture_note: Former cliffside settlement reachable historically only by rope ladders, now accessed by cable car; the name means 'rope' in the local dialect.

name: Rijal Almaa Heritage Village
culture_note: Multi-storey stone tower houses decorated with the traditional Al-Qatt Al-Asiri geometric wall art, a UNESCO-recognized craft.

name: Al-Jabal Al-Akhdar (Green Mountain) Cable Car
culture_note: Cable car climbing above Abha's forested slopes, one of the highest-altitude rides in the Kingdom.

name: Abha Traditional Souq
culture_note: Old-town market for Aseeri honey, coffee, and woven baskets, in the shadow of the historic city wall.

name: Shubra Palace
culture_note: Ottoman-era mansion built in 1905 with Italian marble columns; once used as a residence by King Abdulaziz.

name: Taif Rose Fields
culture_note: Terraced fields growing the Damask rose used in Taif's famous rose water and attar; harvest runs March–April, before sunrise.

name: Al-Hada Mountain Cable Car
culture_note: Cable car descending the escarpment toward Mecca, crossing a road famous for its hairpin switchbacks and resident baboons.

name: Al-Rudaf Park
culture_note: Hilltop public park overlooking the city, popular for picnics in Taif's relatively cool mountain climate.

name: Souq Okaz (Ancient Market Site)
culture_note: One of pre-Islamic Arabia's great annual trade and poetry fairs, held here for centuries before Islam.

name: Al-Shafa Mountain
culture_note: A juniper-forested summer resort area south of Taif, several degrees cooler than the city below.

name: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (Prophet's Mosque)
culture_note: The Prophet Muhammad's mosque and burial site; unlike Mecca's Grand Mosque, its outer courtyards and plazas are open to visitors of all faiths, though the interior prayer halls follow local guidance — check current entry rules before visiting.

name: Quba Mosque
culture_note: Widely regarded as the first mosque built in Islamic history, founded on the Prophet's arrival in Madinah.

name: Mount Uhud
culture_note: Site of the 625 CE Battle of Uhud, one of the formative early battles of Islamic history.

name: Masjid Al-Qiblatain
culture_note: The 'Mosque of the Two Qiblas', where the direction of prayer is said to have changed from Jerusalem to Mecca.

name: Madinah Date Market (Souq Al-Tamr)
culture_note: Madinah is renowned for its date varieties, including Ajwa, sold fresh here near the Prophet's Mosque.

name: Al-Baqi Cemetery (exterior view)
culture_note: Historic cemetery adjacent to the Prophet's Mosque where many of his companions and family are buried; entry is generally restricted, viewed from outside.

name: Dar Al Madinah Museum
culture_note: A local museum tracing the history and urban development of Madinah from before Islam to the present.

name: Masjid al-Haram (The Grand Mosque)
culture_note: Islam's holiest site, home to the Kaaba. Entry to Mecca and the Grand Mosque is restricted to Muslims only — non-Muslim travellers cannot visit the city, and checkpoints on the approach roads enforce this.

name: Jabal al-Nour (Cave of Hira)
culture_note: The mountain holding the cave where Muslims believe the first Quranic revelation occurred; located within Mecca's boundary, which is restricted to Muslims only.

name: Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower
culture_note: One of the world's tallest buildings, standing directly beside the Grand Mosque; like the rest of Mecca, the area is restricted to Muslims only.

name: Dammam Regional Museum
culture_note: Covers the Eastern Province's archaeology and the discovery of oil in Dhahran nearby.

name: Dammam Fish Market (Souq Al-Samak)
culture_note: Working Gulf fish market where the day's catch from Arabian Gulf waters is auctioned each morning.

name: Half Moon Bay
culture_note: Crescent-shaped Gulf beach south of the Dammam-Khobar metro area, a popular weekend swimming and picnic spot.

name: Ithra — King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture
culture_note: Aramco-built cultural complex in Dhahran (not Riyadh) housing a museum, library, cinema, and idea labs in a striking metallic 'tubes' building.

name: Prosperity Well (Dammam Well No. 7)
culture_note: The well that struck oil in commercial quantities in 1938, launching Saudi Arabia's oil industry.

name: Saudi Aramco Exhibit
culture_note: Public exhibition on the history of Saudi Arabia's oil and gas industry, near the original discovery well.

name: Dhahran Techno Valley
culture_note: A research and innovation park adjoining King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals.

name: Dhahran area open desert (Camel viewing)
culture_note: Open desert edging the city where local camel herds are still grazed, a glimpse of the landscape before the oil industry arrived.

name: Al-Khamis Friday Market (Souq Al-Khamis)
culture_note: The city's namesake weekly market — 'Khamis' means Thursday, the traditional trading day for local tribes.

name: Al-Ukhdood Archaeological Site
culture_note: Ruins of an ancient South Arabian city, believed by many scholars to be linked to the Quranic account of the 'People of the Ditch'.

name: Al-Aan Palace (Qasr Al-Emarah)
culture_note: Mudbrick governor's palace showcasing the distinctive vertical mud-tower architecture of Najran's borderland region.

name: Farasan Islands
culture_note: A Red Sea archipelago reached by ferry, known for coral reefs, coastal wildlife, and Ottoman-era coral-stone houses.

name: Fayfa Mountain Coffee Terraces
culture_note: Terraced Khawlani coffee and qat plantations climbing a steep, cloud-forested mountain near the Yemeni border.

name: Abu Arish Old Town
culture_note: Former seat of the Idrisid emirate, with older quarters of traditional Tihama-style mud and thatch houses.

name: Tabuk Castle (Qasr Tabuk)
culture_note: Restored Ottoman fortress that once guarded the pilgrimage and Hejaz Railway route north from Madinah.

name: Old Hejaz Railway Station Tabuk
culture_note: Station on the early 20th-century Ottoman railway linking Damascus to Madinah, later disrupted during the Arab Revolt.

name: Jabal Al-Lawz (Lawz Mountain)
culture_note: One of the Kingdom's highest and coolest mountains, occasionally seeing snow in winter; close to the NEOM development.

name: Tayeb Al-Ism (Blue Lagoon)
culture_note: A turquoise inlet on the Gulf of Aqaba coast, nicknamed the 'Blue Lagoon' for its shallow, mineral-tinted water.

name: Aja and Salma Mountains
culture_note: Twin granite ranges framing Hail, celebrated in pre-Islamic Arabic poetry, most famously that of the poet Hatim al-Tai.

name: Al-Qishlah Historic Fort
culture_note: Late Ottoman-era mudbrick fortress in central Hail, once a garrison and administrative seat.

name: Jubbah Rock Art (UNESCO)
culture_note: Thousands of petroglyphs and inscriptions carved into sandstone outcrops, some dating back over 10,000 years; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2015.

name: Old Yanbu (Yanbu Al-Bahr Historic District)
culture_note: Coral-stone merchant houses in Yanbu's old port quarter, a Red Sea trading town since antiquity.

name: Radhwa Mountain
culture_note: A granite massif inland of Yanbu mentioned in early Islamic-era accounts as a landmark of the western Hejaz.

name: Yanbu Coral Reefs (Sharm Yanbu Diving)
culture_note: Some of the Red Sea's most accessible reef diving, close offshore with visibility often exceeding 20 metres.

name: Yanbu Al-Nakhl Oasis
culture_note: An inland date-palm oasis town along the old pilgrim route, distinct from the coastal industrial city of Yanbu Al-Bahr.
